title: Evaluator Interchange Format (EIF) and Federation Spec
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary

This document defines the Evaluator Interchange Format (EIF) — a compact, versioned JSON schema and federation protocol for exchanging evaluation artifacts across Redwood's eval harness, private runners, Dedicated clusters, and third-party integrators. EIF is designed to: reduce duplication between runners, make regression triage deterministic, enable cross-environment aggregation, and standardize telemetry for quality guardrails and quantization validation.

Goals and non-goals

- Goals:
  - Provide a minimal, unambiguous payload for single-eval results and batch aggregates.
  - Support federation across networks (hosted -> dedicated -> private) with authentication, idempotency, and resumability.
  - Preserve provenance: model version, quantization profile, seed, prompt slice, and evaluator config.
  - Include metric standardization for downstream alerting and regression triage.
- Non-goals:
  - EIF does not attempt to subsume experiment-level metadata stores (e.g., full dataset manifests).
  - EIF is not a general-purpose logging format; it is evaluation-centric.

Scope and audience

- Primary audience: Eval engineers, model onboarding owners, SREs running private/dedicated runners, and applied ML researchers building eval tooling.
- Scope: Single-response and streaming evaluation results, aggregated summaries, and delta (diff) artifacts for regression investigations.

High-level design

1) Versioning
- Top-level field: schema_version (semver, e.g., "1.2.0").
- Backwards-compatible extensions must be additive. Major version bumps imply breaking changes and require migration guidance.

2) Core payload types
- record_type: one of ["sample_result", "batch_summary", "delta_summary", "artifact_reference"].
- sample_result: single prompt -> candidate result + metadata + metrics.
- batch_summary: pre-aggregated metrics (mean, std, sample_count) and histogram references.
- delta_summary: pairwise comparison between two runs for regression triage (includes statistical test outputs).
- artifact_reference: pointer to larger artifacts (audio, debug traces, full conversation logs) stored in object storage with signed URLs.

3) Provenance fields (required)
- run_id: globally unique run identifier (UUID v4).
- evaluator_name: short string (e.g., "answer-fidelity-v2").
- evaluator_version: semantic version used for the evaluator code.
- model: short identifier (catalog/model_id:version).
- model_variant: human-friendly label (e.g., "gpt-like-q4_3b").
- infrastructure: one of ["hosted", "dedicated", "private"] and optional region zone.
- quant_profile: optional label for quantization profile used (e.g., "q8_256k_kv-stable").
- seed: integer seed used when determinism is required (nullable).
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601 UTC timestamp for sample evaluation.

4) Input and prompt metadata
- prompt_id: stable identifier mapped to our prompt canonical store.
- prompt_text: truncated prompt (max 4096 chars); full prompt can be referenced via artifact_reference.
- context_slice: short taxonomy label (e.g., "legal_short_form", "debug_command").
- user_metadata: freeform map permitted as JSON in string-encoded form (max 2048 chars).

5) Output and metrics
- candidate_text: output text (truncated to 16k chars) or reference to artifact.
- metrics: list of metric objects (see example below) describing computed scores. Metric object fields are standardized strings: metric_name, value, unit, aggregator ("raw"|"perplexity"|"score"), sample_weight (float).
- metric_confidence: optional bootstrap/confidence-interval string (e.g., "ci:95:lower=0.45;upper=0.55").

6) Telemetry & observability annotations
- trace_id: optional linking id for distributed tracing.
- runner_id: identifier for the runner instance (hostname/pod).
- sampling_flags: reason why this sample was captured (random, anomaly, adversarial-probe, scheduled).

Example EIF payload (sample_result)

{
  "schema_version": "1.0.0",
  "record_type": "sample_result",
  "run_id": "3f8b1b9a-9c4a-4a0e-9b2d-2b6c3c7e1d16",
  "evaluator_name": "answer-fidelity",
  "evaluator_version": "2.1.0",
  "model": "redwood/consensus-7b:2026-01-13",
  "model_variant": "consensus-7b-q4",
  "infrastructure": "dedicated:us-west-2",
  "quant_profile": "q4_stable_smallkv",
  "seed": 42,
  "timestamp_utc": "2026-02-10T18:23:05Z",
  "prompt_id": "prompts/legal/nda_clause_17",
  "context_slice": "legal_short_form",
  "candidate_text": "The obligation shall not exceed...",
  "metrics": [
    {"metric_name": "exact_match", "value": "0", "unit": "binary", "aggregator": "raw", "sample_weight": "1"},
    {"metric_name": "fidelity_score", "value": "0.72", "unit": "score", "aggregator": "raw", "sample_weight": "1"}
  ]
}

(Full JSON payloads are sent over TLS and may be gzipped for batches.)

Federation protocol

- Transport: HTTPS with JSON-over-POST for small payloads and multipart for artifact references.
- Endpoints: /eif/v{major}/ingest for immediate ingestion, /eif/v{major}/batch for batched uploads, and /eif/v{major}/query to support lightweight aggregations.
- Auth: OAuth2 bearer tokens for Redwood services, mutual TLS available for private peered federation.
- Idempotency: each record may include idempotency_key; ingestion service responds with 409 if duplicate.
- Retry semantics: exponential backoff with jitter. Large batches should use resumable upload protocol (range-based).
- Compression: clients SHOULD gzip large batches and include Content-Encoding header.

Schema compatibility rules

- Additive-only fields are safe in minor versions.
- Renames must create a deprecated alias for one minor release.
- Deprecation policy: mark deprecated in one minor series, remove only on next major bump.

Mapping to Redwood systems

- Ingested EIF sample_result entries are mapped into the eval-metrics warehouse table with columns derived from standard metric_name mappings.
- batch_summary entries are used to populate model-health dashboards and trigger quality-guardrail alerts (see related page: response-stability-index-calibration).
- delta_summary entries feed the automated-regression-bisect pipeline to reduce manual triage time.

Operational SLAs and storage

- Ingest SLA: 99th percentile ingestion latency < 10s for small sample_result POSTs in hosted and dedicated modes.
- Retention: raw EIF payloads retained for 90 days in hot storage, 1 year in cold object storage by default. Policy configurable per account and for private deployments.

Validation and best practices

- Strict schema validation is enforced at the edge; clients get a 422 with an errors array describing missing/invalid fields.
- Use canonical prompt_id where possible to avoid duplicative prompt_text storage.
- Always include quant_profile for runs that use quantized kernels.
- For deterministic evaluations include seed and runner_id.

Security and PII

- Sanitize candidate_text and prompt_text before federation if they may contain PII. Provide redaction flags in the sample_result metadata.
- When storing artifact_reference, prefer object storage with short-lived signed URLs and fine-grained ACLs.

Rollout and migration plan

1. Developer preview: limited to eval-harness internal runners; collect feedback for 2 weeks.
2. Beta: enable ingestion from dedicated clusters; provide an SDK shim for private runners.
3. GA: enable schema_version 1.x in production and deprecate older ingestion paths.

Regression triage playbook (using EIF)

1. Detection: quality-guardrail alert triggers on a delta_summary showing >7% drop in fidelity_score across a slice.
2. Scope: query EIF records for the run_id and prompt slice to retrieve sample_results and artifact references.
3. Hypotheses:
   - Model change (model version/variant mismatch)
   - Quantization effect (quant_profile difference)
   - Prompt drift (prompt_id changed or template altered)
   - Infrastructure noise (runner_id / hardware failures)
4. Bisect: run the automated-regression-bisect pipeline feeding it the delta_summary and sample_result set.
5. Mitigation: pin prior model_variant or fallback to higher-precision quant_profile; deploy hotfix per release runbook.

Tests and QA

- Unit tests: schema round-trip and validation.
- Integration tests: ingestion endpoint with hosted/dedicated/private clients.
- Chaos tests: partial loss of artifact storage and verify resumable uploads.

Ownership and contacts

- Schema and ingestion: team=applied-ml-eval (owner: Aisha Patel).
- Federation infra: eng-platform (primary contact: Marcus Chen).
- Onboarding doc and SDK: eng-developer-experience.

Appendix: minimal metric name whitelist

- fidelity_score, exact_match, rouge_l, bleu, perplexity, embedding_cosine, toxicity_score

Appendix: small config table (plain-text)

- ingestion_endpoint: https://eif.redwood-internal/api/v1/ingest
- batch_endpoint: https://eif.redwood-internal/api/v1/batch
- max_payload_size: 16MB (POST); use batch for larger
- recommended_batch_size: 1000 samples

References and next steps

- Draft SDK (Python/Go) location: internal git repo: //git.redwood/eif-sdk
- Follow-up: create prompt_id canonicalization pipeline and a small CLI for converting legacy eval payloads to EIF.

If you are implementing an evaluator or integrating a runner, start with the Python SDK shim and run the "eif/ci/roundtrip" test. For questions or to request private peering access, contact the federation infra owner on #eif-federation.
